reviews.text: The Samsung Galaxy Book3 is a sleek laptop with a stunning 1920x1080 display that looks vibrant even in bright rooms. Its Intel Core i5 processor handles daily multitasking smoothly, though the 8GB of RAM can feel limiting when running heavy applications. Battery life averages around six hours of mixed use, which is acceptable but not exceptional for a full workday. While the keyboard is comfortable for typing, the trackpad is somewhat small and lacks the precision of premium competitors. Overall, it is a solid mid-range machine with decent build quality, but the price point feels a bit high for the specs offered.

The 15.6-inch display is stunning with vibrant colors and excellent brightness for outdoor use. I was disappointed to find that the battery life barely lasts four hours under normal office tasks. The keyboard feels responsive and the laptop remains lightweight enough for daily commuting. Windows 11 runs smoothly on the Intel Core i5 processor, though the fans get a bit loud during heavy rendering. At this price point, the build quality feels a bit plastic, but it includes plenty of useful ports like USB-C and HDMI.

The keyboard is comfortable for typing, but the trackpad feels slightly slippery compared to my previous Dell. At this price point, I expected more premium build materials, as the chassis feels a bit too plasticky.
